'''Luca Scorrano''' (born September 6, 1971) is an Italian [[biologist]] and professor of Biochemistry at the [[University of Padua]] as well as the former Scientific Director of the Veneto Institute of Molecular Medicine in [[Italy]].<ref name=gs>{{cite web|url= https://scholar.google.lt/citations?user=awFlRz0AAAAJ&hl=en|title=Luca Scorrano|publisher=[[Google Scholar]]|access-date=9 December 2013}}</ref> He is known for his important contributions to the field of mitochondrial dynamics and the interface between mitochondria and the [[endoplasmic reticulum]].

==Biography and research==
Scorrano obtained his M.D. and Ph.D. from the [[University of Padua Medical School]] in 1996 and 2001, respectively. He then moved to [[Boston]] where he worked with [[Stanley J. Korsmeyer]] at [[Harvard Medical School]]. It is during his postdoctoral work in Korsmeyer's lab that Luca became passionate about mitochondrial dynamics and discovered that mitochondrial cristae remodeling was involved in cytochrome c release and apoptosis.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Scorrano|first1=Luca|last2=Ashiya|first2=Mona|last3=Buttle|first3=Karolyn|last4=Weiler|first4=Solly|last5=Oakes|first5=Scott A.|last6=Mannella|first6=Carmen A.|last7=Korsmeyer|first7=Stanley J.|date=January 2002|title=A distinct pathway remodels mitochondrial cristae and mobilizes cytochrome c during apoptosis|journal=Developmental Cell|volume=2|issue=1|pages=55–67|doi=10.1016/s1534-5807(01)00116-2|issn=1534-5807|pmid=11782314|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2003 he returned to Italy to establish his lab at the University of Padua, and then in Geneva (Switzerland) where he was Professor at the Dept. of Cell Physiology and Metabolism. In 2013 he returned to his native Italy where he continued to unravel the molecular mechanisms of mitochondrial dynamics and their pathophysiological consequences.

He has been prolific in his contributions to the fields of apoptosis and mitochondrial pathophysiology,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cipolat|first1=Sara|last2=Rudka|first2=Tomasz|last3=Hartmann|first3=Dieter|last4=Costa|first4=Veronica|last5=Serneels|first5=Lutgarde|last6=Craessaerts|first6=Katleen|last7=Metzger|first7=Kristine|last8=Frezza|first8=Christian|last9=Annaert|first9=Wim|last10=D'Adamio|first10=Luciano|last11=Derks|first11=Carmen|date=14 July 2006|title=Mitochondrial rhomboid PARL regulates cytochrome c release during apoptosis via OPA1-dependent cristae remodeling|journal=Cell|volume=126|issue=1|pages=163–175|doi=10.1016/j.cell.2006.06.021|issn=0092-8674|pmid=16839884|s2cid=6396519|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Scorrano|first1=Luca|last2=Ashiya|first2=Mona|last3=Buttle|first3=Karolyn|last4=Weiler|first4=Solly|last5=Oakes|first5=Scott A.|last6=Mannella|first6=Carmen A.|last7=Korsmeyer|first7=Stanley J.|date=January 2002|title=A distinct pathway remodels mitochondrial cristae and mobilizes cytochrome c during apoptosis|journal=Developmental Cell|volume=2|issue=1|pages=55–67|doi=10.1016/s1534-5807(01)00116-2|issn=1534-5807|pmid=11782314|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Frezza|first1=Christian|last2=Cipolat|first2=Sara|last3=Martins de Brito|first3=Olga|last4=Micaroni|first4=Massimo|last5=Beznoussenko|first5=Galina V.|last6=Rudka|first6=Tomasz|last7=Bartoli|first7=Davide|last8=Polishuck|first8=Roman S.|last9=Danial|first9=Nika N.|last10=De Strooper|first10=Bart|last11=Scorrano|first11=Luca|date=14 July 2006|title=OPA1 controls apoptotic cristae remodeling independently from mitochondrial fusion|journal=Cell|volume=126|issue=1|pages=177–189|doi=10.1016/j.cell.2006.06.025|issn=0092-8674|pmid=16839885|s2cid=11569831|doi-access=free}}</ref> as well as mitochondrial dynamics and interorganellar contact sites. His lab is now focused on understanding the molecular mechanisms and pathophysiological consequences of mitochondrial dynamics and contacts with the ER in health and disease.

==Awards==
Scorrano received several prizes and awards, including the Eppendorf European Young Investigator, the Chiara D’Onofrio and the ESCI Award. He is an EMBO Member and sits in several Committees, Advisory and Editorial Boards.
